notes: Scope: the Applied Systems bundle (127 answers) contains the 111 EZLynx answers because EZLynx is an alias in the release matching rule. Following the brief (a statement belongs to the vendor whose bundle is being coded and is classed against that vendor's own pages), this file codes statements about Applied Systems and its Applied-branded products (Applied Epic) plus the Applied to EZLynx ownership and acquisition statements; statements about the EZLynx product itself (its prices, plans, integrations, platforms) are coded in the EZLynx file against ezlynx.com and are not repeated here. Five own pages read on www1.appliedsystems.com, all HTTP 200 and not thin. Every price figure for Applied Epic is unverifiable: no page read publishes a price, and the product page only offers contact with sales. Not coded: review ratings and G2 reviewer counts, market share figures (an IIABA survey percentage), hedged or hypothetical cost lines (a 10-user setup could cost $30,000 a year; potential hidden implementation fees; hypothetical premium examples), fit opinions, and the Indio and TAM mentions in answers that do not present them as Applied products. No claim is wrong or stale, so no cited page was read for causes. Pass 2 (8 Oct 2026): no browser reads exist for this vendor and no claim was unverifiable because of a blocked or thin page (all unverifiable claims are prices Applied does not publish), so nothing was re-classed and no page was added. Gap lines naming Applied products were fit opinions, feature lists, generic criteria (IVANS or API carrier connectivity) or statements about other vendors (InsuredMine's integration list, NowCerts pricing); the remaining gap lines are about EZLynx and belong to the EZLynx file. Sub-heading pricing lines under Applied Epic in Claude q2 runs 1 and 3 added instances: q2 Claude run 3 to C02; q2 Claude runs 1 and 3 to C07 and C09; q2 Claude run 1 to C12. Comparison tables with Applied Epic as a column header (q8 Claude runs 1 to 3) carry only prices already coded for those answers (C05, C09), ratings and fit rows. No claim is wrong or stale, so the consistency check changed nothing.
